summary: This document is a research discussion card (N4) proposing a reanalysis/future experiment to test whether ³¹P-MRS phosphocreatine (PCr) is a superior pharmacodynamic biomarker over plasma creatine for oral creatine's cognitive/working-memory rescue under sleep restriction. It is classified as NEGATIVE (kills the blood-creatine-as-PD narrative) and is at TRL 1–2: the core subject-level covariance claim is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN, with supporting literature at group/condition level only. No new experiments are reported; the document synthesizes existing literature and defines a prediction/pre-registration framework.

content_blocks.title: Document Header & Classification
content_blocks.content: Card ID: N4. Title: 'Sleep-restriction cognition tracks ³¹P-MRS PCr, not plasma creatine.' Status: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative). Lane: nootropics. Risk class: research-discussion. Novelty: biomarker-bridge. Method: propose-reanalysis. OpenLabs target: discussion (PASS_NEGATIVE — not claim). IP class: biomarker-bridge; vault_hold=no; kill_cost_tier=1; time_to_refute=4 weeks.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: Under sleep restriction, oral-creatine cognitive/working-memory benefit is NOT adequately indexed by plasma (or serum) creatine. A pre-registered subject-level contrast must show WM (or processing-speed) Δ covaries more strongly with ³¹P-MRS PCr or PCr/Pi than with plasma creatine. Quantitative threshold: |r_WM,PCr| − |r_WM,plasmaCr| ≥ 0.20, OR plasma-alone mediation fails while PCr mediation holds. This is a PREDICTION, not an observed result.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Sleep loss shifts gray-matter and thalamic PCr on ³¹P-MRS. Oral creatine under ~21 h deprivation moves cognition with PCr/Pi and ATP at group/condition level. Oral creatine can raise brain total creatine on ¹H-MRS. McMorris-era SD cognition trials report catecholamines/cortisol, not plasma creatine, as the cognitive covariate. Subject-level WM~PCr vs WM~plasma creatine head-to-head covariance remains UNTESTED.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Plasma/serum creatine rise is an adequate primary PD/biomarker bridge for oral creatine's WM or cognitive rescue under sleep restriction.

Baseline measured (literature-supported):
- SD+creatine moves cognition with ³¹P-MRS HEP/PCr at GROUP level (PMID 38418482; 40520504)
- SD alone alters cerebral PCr (PMID 25325507; PMID 30282723)
- Oral creatine raises brain tCr (PMID 10484486)
- SD cognition creatine trials without plasma-Cr PD (PMID 16416332)
- Plasma Cr × cognition × sleep-restriction PubMed hits = 0
- Subject-level WM~PCr vs WM~plasmaCr covariance/mediation superiority: UNKNOWN
- |Δr| ≥ 0.20 concordance rule: PREDICTION only

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Parallel group effects ≠ proven subject-level covariance — Gordji shows co-movement; PCr-over-plasma superiority still UNKNOWN.
2. Plasma creatine is under-measured in SD×cognition designs, not experimentally falsified.
3. Endpoint breadth — batteries mix PVT/processing speed/executive/digit span; one primary endpoint must be locked before claiming WM.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis (Critical Dependencies)
content_blocks.content:
Three ablation conditions that would invalidate the card:
1. Remove ³¹P-MRS PCr/HEP as brain-side PD arm → Cannot prefer brain HEP over plasma; only restates that creatine can help SD cognition.
2. Remove plasma creatine as competing blood PD (explicit contrast or mediation fail) → Showing WM~PCr alone does not kill the popular blood-creatine-PD narrative.
3. Remove sleep-restriction/sleep-deprivation context → Resting WM or vegetarian digit-span creatine effects (e.g., Rae) are a different claim class without the SD bioenergetic bridge.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: The claim is refuted if: In a pre-registered sleep-restriction panel with paired ³¹P-MRS and plasma creatine, plasma creatine matches or exceeds PCr as a subject-level correlate/mediator of WM (or locked cognitive primary) — i.e., |r_WM,plasmaCr| ≥ |r_WM,PCr| OR plasma mediation holds while PCr does not (blood-Cr PD survives).

content_blocks.title: Open Questions / Human Review Request
content_blocks.content: Lock primary cognitive endpoint (WM task vs PVT/processing speed), MRS voxel, and plasma vs serum creatine assay before claiming any blood PD; no dosing recommendation. Peer-review invited. Document is literature/computational prediction for research discussion only. Not medical advice. Not a dosing or treatment recommendation.

key_findings: Core claim is a PREDICTION, not an observed result: subject-level WM~PCr vs WM~plasma creatine covariance under sleep restriction is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN.

Group-level literature supports PCr/HEP co-movement with cognition under ~21 h sleep deprivation + oral creatine (Gordji-Nejad 2024, PMID 38418482; 2025, PMID 40520504), but subject-level mediation/correlation superiority of PCr over plasma creatine has not been tested.
PubMed scout search returns 0 hits for plasma creatine × cognition × sleep deprivation/restriction — plasma creatine as a PD biomarker in this context is entirely unestablished.
Acute sleep deprivation alters gray-matter PCr on ³¹P-MRS independent of supplementation (Dorsey, PMID 25325507).
Oral creatine raises brain total creatine on quantitative ¹H-MRS in healthy volunteers (Dechent, PMID 10484486).
Quantitative threshold for claim validation: |r_WM,PCr| − |r_WM,plasmaCr| ≥ 0.20 (pre-registered, subject-level), or plasma-alone mediation null while PCr mediation significant.
Time-to-refute estimated at 4 weeks (kill_cost_tier=1), suggesting low experimental cost to test.
No new experimental data are presented; document is a research discussion/reanalysis proposal synthesizing existing literature.
TRL assessment: TRL 1–2 (basic concept with supporting literature at group level; no subject-level or head-to-head biomarker data exist).
